assertion.statement: Every elliptic curve A/Q of arithmetic conductor N is modular and admits a finite surjective Q-morphism X0(N) to A.
assertion.objects: The actual elliptic curve A/Q, its arithmetic conductor N and its conductor-level modular parametrization.
assertion.hypotheses: A is an elliptic curve over Q.
assertion.quantifiers: Every elliptic curve over Q; no semistability, residual-image or non-CM restriction.
assertion.parameter_range: Arithmetic conductor N of the same A, not an arbitrary enlarged level.
assertion.uniformity: Qualitative existence for each A; no effective degree bound.
assertion.normalizations: Published Silverman second edition C.13.6 and C.16.4(a),(c); BCDT attribution retained.
assertion.exceptional_cases: C.16.4(b) Fricke formula excluded. No normalized newform, optimality, Manin constant or Hecke identity inferred.
assertion.limit_order: Choose A and its conductor, then its parametrization before forming later quotient maps.

base_use.reason: Both the arbitrary forward-rank elliptic curve and the actual RC curve are over Q. The universal published formulation applies directly at their arithmetic conductors.
base_use.shared_contract_justification: The same universal theorem is instantiated for the arbitrary forward-rank A/Q and the fixed RC E_l/Q. Neither instance needs or supplies the other instance; their later quotient constructions remain distinct. The universal elliptic-curve statement is applied to the same actual quadratic twist E^h/Q at both invocations of forward-rank. Nonzero normalized L_*(h) implies L(E^h,1) nonzero because the retained period and omitted factors are nonzero. Modularity, rank0/full Sha finiteness and then full two-primary Selmer corank0 are consumed in that order; no converse or new local bound is asserted.

supplier.statement: Every elliptic curve A/Q of arithmetic conductor N is modular and admits a finite surjective Q-morphism X0(N) to A.

assertion.statement: For the stated finite curve morphism, divisor pushforward preserves degree and principal divisors; the identity point identifies the elliptic degree-zero divisor-class group with A.
assertion.objects: Geometric divisors and degree-zero divisor classes on the stated smooth curves and elliptic A.
assertion.hypotheses: Finite morphism of smooth curves and identity point on elliptic A.
assertion.quantifiers: Every actual elliptic curve A/Q satisfying the stated hypotheses.
assertion.parameter_range: The fixed geometric divisor groups and finite map.
assertion.uniformity: Qualitative statement for each A; no effective bound.
assertion.constants: No numerical constant or effective bound.
assertion.normalizations: Geometric divisor-class groups; coefficient one for pushforward of a geometric point.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No assertion that rational line bundles equal all rational Picard points. Picard representability, norm base change, and the algebraic quotient are separate inputs and deductions.
assertion.limit_order: Pass divisors to divisor classes before the separate algebraic Picard construction.
